chief_complaint: lower back stiffness and pain since yesterday
hpi_details: felt a sudden twinge in her lower back yesterday afternoon while lifting heavy moving boxes. The pain is a dull, constant ache across the lower back, worse when bending or sitting for long. No radiation to the legs, no numbness or tingling, no weakness. Normal bowel and bladder function.
ideas: thinks she strained a muscle while lifting the boxes incorrectly
concerns: worried that she might have damaged her spine or slipped a disc
expectations: wants to know if she needs an X-ray or a scan, and if she should stay in bed
medications: took one ibuprofen tablet this morning, helped slightly
social_hx: works as a school teacher, active lifestyle, non-smoker

learning_objectives: Practise assessing acute musculoskeletal pain (onset, character, radiation, relieving/aggravating factors)
Screen for red flags (numbness, weakness, bowel/bladder changes)
Provide reassurance and explain that scans are not usually needed for simple muscle strains
Advise on active recovery (avoiding prolonged bed rest) using clear, simple English
suggested_questions: What were you doing when the pain started?
Does the pain go down your legs at all?
Have you noticed any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your legs?
Have you had any changes in your bowel or bladder control?
Does anything make the pain feel better or worse?
What are you most worried about regarding this pain?
